Correct, and this can't be fixed reliably on the client: the run-grouping needs a full run, but the API paginates *raw attempts* (25/page), so any run straddling a page boundary is only partially visible and gets reconstructed as two partial runs — with polling offset shifts making it worse. A client-side heuristic would still be wrong across the boundary.

The right fix is run-aware pagination in the delivery-history API/store (paginate by `webhook_id`/run rather than by raw attempt, and return each run's attempts together). That lives in the history-store layer, not this UI PR. Tracking it there as a follow-up; leaving the client grouping as-is since it's correct within a page.

Known limitation, same root cause as the earlier thread on this file: run-grouping needs a full run, but the delivery-history API paginates *raw attempts* (25/page), so a run straddling a page boundary can't be regrouped correctly on the client. The correct fix is run-aware pagination in the history API/store (paginate by webhook_id/run and return each run's attempts together), which lives in the history-store layer, not this UI PR. Tracking it there; the client grouping is correct within a page.

The webhook endpoint API has no revision/ETag field, and PUT is intentionally a full-state replace (documented: redacted header values round-trip untouched and the server keeps the stored secret). Adding optimistic-concurrency (If-Match/revision) is a server-side API change, out of scope for this UI PR. Noting it for the API layer; the UI resends full state by design so toggles and edits carry the complete row.
